account: HM Revenue & Customs launched Connect in 2010–11. Its annual report calls it an IT system that joins a billion pieces of data across its tax regimes to help identify fraud. In a freedom-of-information response reported by Pinsent Masons on 8 October 2025, HMRC said Connect cases generated an average £3.4 billion of additional annual yield. It was about £4.6 billion in 2024–25, with around 4,300 staff using it. The Comptroller and Auditor General's report in HMRC's 2024–25 accounts records that HMRC used TRUCE (Transaction Risking Upstream in a Connect Environment). It served to identify and stop VAT and income-tax repayments needing investigation. IDRS replaced it from August 2023. Official sources describe data analytics and risk rules, not AI.

ai_role.statement: Yield attribution to Connect comes from HMRC's FOI response as reported by Pinsent Masons. No independent evaluation apportions yield between the system and caseworkers. The NAO's audit report describes TRUCE/IDRS as automated risk-assessment of repayment claims whose controls it reviewed, without quantifying stopped repayments. The cited sources describe the system as data analytics and risk rules rather than machine learning.

fields.account: HM Revenue & Customs launched Connect in 2010–11. Its annual report calls it an IT system that joins a billion pieces of data across its tax regimes to help identify fraud. In a freedom-of-information response reported by Pinsent Masons on 8 October 2025, HMRC said Connect cases generated an average £3.4 billion of additional annual yield. It was about £4.6 billion in 2024–25, with around 4,300 staff using it. The Comptroller and Auditor General's report in HMRC's 2024–25 accounts records that HMRC used TRUCE (Transaction Risking Upstream in a Connect Environment). It served to identify and stop VAT and income-tax repayments needing investigation. IDRS replaced it from August 2023. Official sources describe data analytics and risk rules, not AI.

title: HMRC's Connect data-matching system: about £4.6 billion of additional yield in 2024–25

value.quote: HMRC, in a freedom of information request to Pinsent Masons, said it generated on average £3.4bn in additional annual yield from Connect cases, with the 2024-25 tax year generating approximately £4.6bn.
value.what: additional tax yield from Connect cases in the 2024-25 tax year (average £3.4bn a year)
